title: Generalize triangle removal to K_r-removal process

problemStatement.formal: For r \geq 3, define the K_r-removal process on K_n: repeatedly remove all edges of a uniformly random r-clique until the graph is K_r-free. Let f_r(n) be the expected remaining edge count. Conjecture: there exist constants 0 < c_1 \leq c_2 such that c_1 n^{\alpha} \leq f_r(n) \leq c_2 n^{\alpha} for all large n, where \alpha = 2 - 2/(r+1).
problemStatement.plain: Generalize the triangle removal process (Erdős #1155, BFL 2015) to K_r-cliques for r \geq 3. The conjectured exponent is 2-2/(r+1): equals 3/2 for r=3 (BFL), 8/5 for r=4, 5/3 for r=5, and approaches 2 as r \to \infty.
whyMatters: Generalizes BFL (2015) f_3(n) = n^{3/2 + o(1)} to arbitrary r-cliques
Connects random combinatorial processes to Kruskal-Katona-type thresholds
Provides clean structural framework: exponent is strictly monotone in r, bounded in [1,2)
Decomposes into modular subgoals (upper Theta, lower Theta, ratio convergence)

proven: Exponent 2-2/(r+1) is strictly monotone increasing in r and bounded in [1, 2)
Conjecture is equivalent to upper Theta-bound AND lower Theta-bound (decomposition)
Conjecture follows from convergence f_r(n)/n^{\alpha} \to L > 0
Conjecture implies BFL-type sub-polynomial bound n^{\alpha \pm \epsilon}
open: K_r-removal conjecture for any r \geq 4 (no rigorous proof exists)
Whether the BFL (2015) machinery generalizes or fundamentally new tools are required
Connection between K_r-removal rate and Ramsey multiplicity in dense graphs
knownResults.goal: Prove f_r(n) \asymp n^{2-2/(r+1)} for some r \geq 4 (e.g., r = 4 case: f_4(n) \asymp n^{8/5}).

currentState.focus: Generalization framework formalized; awaiting future work on r \geq 4 tight bounds.
currentState.nextAction: Future researcher: attempt r = 4 BFL-style proof or investigate Ramsey-multiplicity connection.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Created full K_r-removal generalization with 3 axioms, 0 sorries. Defines the generalized process, proves exponent properties (monotonicity, bounds, computed values), states conjecture and BFL-type bound, proves equivalence characterizations.
builtItems: Erdos1155OQ01OQ07.lean: K_r-removal generalization (3 axioms, 0 sorries, ~240 lines)
kRemovalExponent: computable exponent function with verified values for r=3,4,5
insights: Generalized triangle removal to K_r-removal for arbitrary r >= 3
Conjectured exponent is 2-2/(r+1): yields 3/2 for r=3 (BFL), 8/5 for r=4, 5/3 for r=5
Exponent is strictly monotone in r and approaches 2 as r -> infinity
The conjecture decomposes into independent upper and lower Theta-bounds (same as r=3 case)
Ratio convergence f_r(n)/n^alpha -> L > 0 is a sufficient condition for the conjecture
nextSteps: Prove tight exponent for r=4 (K_4-removal) analogous to BFL for r=3
Connect K_r-removal rates to Ramsey multiplicity

papers: Bohman, T., Fonoberova, M., Lladó, A. (2015). The triangle-free process and the Ramsey number R(3,k). Memoirs of the AMS / arXiv:1302.5963 — proves f_3(n) = n^{3/2 + o(1)}.
Erdős, P., Suen, S., Winkler, P. (1995). On the size of a random maximal graph. Random Structures & Algorithms — early analysis of the triangle removal process.
